interest: Japanese penetration of Davao and Dutch intelligence sharing on the eve of war.
overview: State Department decimal file 894.20211B (File 1162) documents U.S. diplomatic and intelligence monitoring of Japanese military, political, and economic activities in the Philippine Islands during the 1930s. The file includes cross-reference sheets concerning War Department and State Department records on Japanese national grievances and propaganda in the Commonwealth; consular despatches and Hong Kong press clippings analyzing Japanese economic penetration of Davao Province, where extensive hemp investments and legal stratagems using Hawaii-born Japanese to acquire public lands caused acute concern; correspondence acknowledging FBI reports on subversive activities; and a detailed despatch from the American Consulate General in Batavia reporting a request from the Netherlands East Indies government for American intelligence on Japanese infiltration in the Philippines to complete a comprehensive map of Japanese penetration throughout the 'South Seas' (Nanyo).

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Hornbeck Memorandum on Japanese Propaganda in the Philippines

subfiles.about: Internal State Department summary slip reviewing a Hong Kong consular despatch on Chinese reports of Japanese economic penetration in Davao.

subfiles.title: State Department Summary Slip on Hong Kong Despatch Regarding Japanese Activities in Davao

subfiles.about: Consular despatch transmitting a South China Morning Post report on Japanese economic penetration in Davao and potential evasion of Philippine land ownership laws by Hawaii-born Japanese.

subfiles.summary: Donovan forwards a press report on Japanese expansion in Davao, including Hawaii-born Japanese acquiring land restricted to foreigners.
subfiles.title: Despatch from American Consul Howard Donovan (Hong Kong) on Japanese Activities in the Philippines

subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.title: Letter from Assistant Secretary George S. Messersmith to FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover Regarding Subversive Activities
subfiles.to: John Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting a request from Dutch East Indies official A. H. J. Lovink for U.S. intelligence on Japanese penetration of the Philippines to complete a South Seas intelligence chart.
subfiles.from: Erle R. Dickover, American Consul General, Batavia, Java
subfiles.summary: Dickover reports that Dutch adviser A. H. J. Lovink asked for data on Japanese activities in the Philippines to complete a chart of Japanese networks in the South Seas.
